locations.label: Warms (or cools) skin/orange tones only — everything else is unaffected. Dial to taste; not a color-accuracy control.

Cuts atmospheric haze in the distance — extra contrast/black-point/saturation, but only where the image reads BRIGHT and DESATURATED (a hazy sky or ridge), so foreground color is left alone. Negative values add haze back in.
Capture sharpening — RAW photos default to 40 on load/reset (moved here so it survives Reset independently of the general Adjust sliders).
Blend between the original and the deconvolved result.
Size of the assumed lens/sensor blur (Gaussian PSF) to invert.
Lifts/lowers the darkest tones.
Lifts/lowers the low-midtones.
Lifts/lowers the high-midtones.
Lifts/lowers the brightest tones.
How wide a neighborhood of similar colors around the picked point is affected — low = only close matches, high = a broad spread of nearby hues/saturations
Overrides EXIF auto-detection with a lens you pick directly — for manual/adapted lenses that write no lens EXIF at all. Picking one also turns Auto on.
Focal length in mm — required for distortion correction. Auto-filled for fixed (prime) lenses.
Straightens bowed lines. Positive fixes barrel distortion (lines bow outward), negative fixes pincushion (lines bow inward).
Brightens the corners to counteract lens vignetting.
Corrects red/blue fringing near high-contrast edges, worst in the corners.
Corrects converging verticals — the building-shot lean. A true perspective correction, so spacing stays right instead of just straightening the edges.
Same correction on the horizontal axis, for a wall or facade shot from one side.
Fine rotation, in tenths of a degree — for levelling a horizon without leaving the panel.
Zooms in to hide the empty wedges a perspective correction leaves at the frame edge.

Removes purple/green color fringes on high-contrast edges — the local fringing that survives the geometric CA correction above, or that a fast lens makes wide open. Gated on edges, so flat purple or green subjects are left alone.
Swap the picked aspect ratio between portrait and landscape (e.g. 3:2 ↔ 2:3) — the chip list above only lists one orientation each.
Constrains where Auto level looks for a line — useful when a stronger false line elsewhere in the frame (a wave, a shoreline fragment) keeps outscoring the real horizon.
Fine-tune the grain clump size on top of the film format (5 = format-accurate).
Dehancer film-format grain: smaller formats are coarser/stronger, 65mm is the finest & weakest.
0 = grain frozen to the screen. 100 = fully independent every frame (can boil at high Amount). Real film sits in between.
Sub-pixel frame-to-frame wobble, the way a projector gate holds film. A little goes a long way — past about 30 it reads as a shaky camera rather than a projector.
Per-frame exposure flicker, the way a projector lamp and shutter never deliver exactly the same light twice.
Random dust specks and the odd hair — mostly light (dust on the negative prints white).
Thin vertical emulsion scratches with a gentle wobble.
A warm light leak flooding in from one edge.
1 = photo fits the canvas exactly; smaller = more matte around it; bigger = crops into the frame.
JPG is never fully lossless, even at 100. PNG is lossless but files are much larger.
Never enlarges — a target above the photo's own long edge is ignored.
Applied last, after the resize — the only point at which the right amount is knowable.
Writes a HEIC whose base image is this grade and whose gain map carries the highlight detail the camera captured. HDR displays show the extra range; everything else sees the normal SDR image.
Draws a translucent text watermark into the bottom-right corner of the exported file only — never the on-screen preview.
Also upload every export to a "Chromasmith" album in your Google Photos
Trim in/out — used at export and to bound loop playback

Apple Photos-style: suppress a Find result below this raw similarity instead of always applying it. Off by default — score cannot reliably tell a hit from a miss (subject.rs measures both around 0.70-0.79), so treat this as a personal tolerance, not a real confidence cutoff.

How far apart two candidates must be to count as separate instances rather than the same subject\'s own neighbouring cells. Tighten for a litter of small, closely-packed subjects; loosen for two large ones.
Most instances to look for.

Restricts this mask to pixels near the picked tones, so a rough shape can still land on one subject only. Combine with the shape to exclude same-coloured objects (pets, wood, sand).
Restricts this mask to a near/far band of the photo\'s estimated depth.
Darkens and saturates the selected coat — the classic \'deep, rich colour\' move (lower exposure, higher saturation), scaled by one strength.
Brightens and opens shadow detail inside this mask — drag the ellipse on the photo onto the eye(s) first, this only controls how strong the brightening is.
How far the selected tones move toward the target — a CONVERGENCE, not a shift.
Measured mean of the selection, and what it converges toward.
Measured mean of the '+subjWord+' actually selected (not just your picks), and the target Depth/Warmth resolve to. A guide, not a guarantee — per-pixel results also depend on Preserve and Strength.
How far the selected tones move toward the target. This is a CONVERGENCE, not a shift: uneven areas even out instead of the darkest simply getting darker.
0 collapses lightness onto the target — it evens out a tan LINE but flattens the shading that gives a body its form. 100 shifts the overall level with shading fully intact.
Negative softens detail inside the mask (skin), positive sharpens it. Works on fine detail only — it does not change tone or color.
Pick any color to tint the masked area toward — the hue slider below fine-tunes it.
